newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN INFLATIONARY EXPECTS UP SLIGHTLY IN AUG.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN INFLATIONARY EXPECTS UP SLIGHTLY IN AUG.

text.p: Australian consumers' inflationary expectations rose slightly in August to 3.4 percent from 3.3 percent in July, the Melbourne Institute found.
Expectations have hovered around 4.0 percent for the past five years, but over the past 12 months, median expectations of of price rises have declined by 0.9 percentage points.
The Institute said while this was a significant delcine, with expectations now at historical lows, the actual rate of underlying inflation had fallen by 1.4 percentage points in the the year to June.

The Institute found that households earning less than A$20,000 were predicting inflation to be around 4.7 percent compared to expectations of inflation between 2.7 and 3.2 percent from households with incomes of more than A$41,000.

"Part of the reason for this divergence may be a result of lower income earners watching individual prices more carefully, and therefore being less influenced by movements in official consumer price index (CPI) measures," the Insitute said.

Renters had higher inflationary expectations than home owners, which the Institute said may reflect the fact that those with a property keep a closer eye on the CPI as this has an impact on house prices and mortgage repayments.
